Made this account on the day of the exodus, but you know, unintended DDoS from us, intentional DDoS from elsewhere and so on.

I wanted to give some first impressions of Voat. I'm a software developer and used to enjoy Reddit for the last 5 years. Although I did not care for fatpeoplehate or the other casualties, I can see the direction Reddit is headed in, and I don't like it. /v/conspiracy ended up being right, go figure.

Okay. Voat. Can't help comparing to Reddit for obvious reasons. This is what I found so far:

Good:

  • Dark theme. Fuck yeah. This is by far the biggest plus and a big fat one-up on Reddit. There's a reason many developers use dark themes whenever possible. A bright white screen is pretty, but comes with a headache and hurting eyes.
  • Generally pretty. The design makes it feel a bit less dated than Reddit, although not super fancy. Keeping it simple means nice usability.
  • Seemingly not aimed at investors yet. Of course no-one makes a site like this without a purpose, but unlike Reddit, it seems Voat cares for their users. This changed for Reddit, let's hope we don't repeat that.
  • Freedom to create fatpeoplehate and everything else that's offensive.
  • Better interface for posting discussions, mainly the toolbar to format your text.
  • Raw vote indicator. No shitty hiding. We see exactly how many ups and downs.
  • Embedded video player in comments and visual identification of links. Yes, i hate when I'm taken to YouTube at inappropriate times.

Bad:

  • Small community. Some are going to like it. I don't. Reddit has massive amount of subs for everything, and so much activity.
  • No image host. Imgur is too close to Reddit for me to like it. But I read that it might be looked into in the future, so no worries, we can wait.
  • Odd name. Voat. It's growing on me because goats, but I don't know. It seems like it is trying a bit too hard to be catchy. Better than WhoaVerse though.
  • Missing/worse features. For example I liked trending subreddits because we had 5 new every day.

I'll find more pros and cons, but you're off to a good start Voat. Bookmarked, bitches!

Now I'm sure most of the anime fans are already highly familiar with this particular anime. However for those who still have not seen this masterpiece I can highly recommend it to you.

The basic plot is that everyone finds themselves in the afterlife, with a twist, the twist being that they are stuck in some kind of Limbo. This is all I'm going to say about the story because I don't want to spoil anything.

The animation is beautifully executed, the characters are funny and remarkable. The show manages to combine action, comedy and some romance in a perfect mix so that nothing gets left out. The soundtrack is amazing.

Sadly due to budget constraints the studio that made Angel Beats was forced to cut it down to only 13 episodes out of the planned 24. This led to some of the main cast not having proper backgrounds and just not enough screentime. However even with the budget contraints I would still put up Angel Beats among the top anime that ever existed. On MyAnimeList it is ranked #116 even though it came out in mid 2010.

So please, do yourself a favour and go watch it. It's only 13 episodes that are about 20 minutes each. But you'll probably find yourself still thinking over it long after you have finished watching.

I'll make a second recommendation off of your own.

If you're a fan of romance/action, or in general enjoy well written series, then this is definitely a show to watch. However if you absolutely despise the "moe" anime style, then you should probably step away now. If you want to see something entirely new and have it explore uncharted territory, you should also probably step away now.

By no means is Angel Beats revolutionary, nor is it the first to do anything. It has a lot of the familiar character tropes (the term "Haruhi clone" is just simply too fitting), and a lot of familiar cliches. Its strength is instead in putting together a well thought out world ad populating it with characters who are developed well enough to have their own motives, dreams, and desires. In short, it excels at doing a lot of the same things that a lot of other shows have already done.

The writing is exceptionally good, with minor details that seem inconsequential when they happen (e.g.) later being revealed to be either plot important or important to character development (e.g.). Perhaps most important is the fact that the show's writing is good at drawing in a level of emotional involvement for the characters, which frequently leads to emotional whiplash early on when the show jerks from beautifully animated action scenes to tragic character backstories. The whiplash tends to become less frequent as the series truly gets into stride and

Overall, here is how I'd rate the show:

Concept: 6/10. Lot of stuff seen here before, but putting them all together in one package was definitely new.

Writing: 8/10. Still uses a lot of cliches, but it definitely makes up for that with impressive writing and emotional rapport later on.

Characters: 8/10. Again, uses a lot of cliches, but they are well developed and well rounded.

Aesthetics: 10/10. If you're not a fan of the moe art-style, you're going to immediately disagree with me. But the animation (especially the action sequences) is so beautifully done and polished, that it feels remarkably clean. The music is also incredibly good.

Execution: 9/10. There are a few falters, but otherwise the show is beautifully put together which each element adding something and creating a wonderful balance.

Overall: 8.2/10. It's great.

Like I said, but I have to say it again, the music is also exceptional. It is so exceptional that Wikipedia dedicated it's own page to it and that in Japan Girls Dead Monster (the band featured in the anime) had their own tour, AKA the voice actress who was responsible for the singing.

I thought AB was alright, but it could have been so much more. The premise itself was great, but it jumped between so many distinctly different parts of the story and it didn't really feel like any of it fit together that well, like the control room scene, or the forced romance. I left feeling that nothing was particularly well explained, although I hope some of the shortcomings present in the anime are addressed in the upcoming VN.
